requested.title: Tar entry names are joined onto the output directory with no containment check (tar slip)
Every non-mochi `workspace:*` dependency is silently rewritten to the public-registry `latest`
Neither network call has a timeout, and `fetchLatestMochiVersion`'s `signal` parameter is dead code
Three of four prompts lack the non-TTY guard that `promptToggle` documents as necessary
Unauthenticated SSE and deliberately-slow API endpoints with no rate limit, no request timeout, and no stream backpressure
Internet-facing demos deployment runs with `development: true`, leaking stack traces and mounting dev-only internal routes
`proxy.origin` silently falls back to `http://localhost:${PORT}` when MOCHI_ORIGIN is unset, with no boot-time check

parsedVerdicts.reasoning: The missing control is real and the mechanism is confirmed from Bun's own documentation and typings, not inferred. `/docs/runtime/archive` attaches its security note explicitly to extraction ('Bun.Archive validates paths during extraction… normalizes away path traversal components (`..`)'), while the `files()` JSDoc in `node_modules/bun-types/bun.d.ts` promises only that keys are 'file paths (always using forward slashes `/` as separators)' — no absolute-path rejection, no `..` normalization — and the docs' own 'additional security with untrusted archives' example tells you to enumerate `files()` and validate the paths yourself. `extractTemplate` (download.ts:33-46) does none of that: `root` is the entry's own first segment, `relative` is a fixed-length slice, and `Bun.write(path.join(dir, relative), file)` writes it unchecked, so an entry `mochi-HEAD/packages/minimal/../../../../x` matches the `*/packages/minimal/**` glob (the suite's own fixture proves dot-prefixed segments survive the glob, since `.gitignore` is extracted) and escapes `dir`. I confirmed the slice arithmetic itself is sound and that no caller-side validation exists anywhere in cli.ts/create.ts/utils.ts, and that no fix has landed (last commit touching these files predates the finding). Exploitability is genuinely gated, as the finding concedes: `tarballUrl()` hardcodes HTTPS to codeload for a hardcoded `khromov/mochi/...` source (templates.ts:14-27, and cli.ts restricts `--template` to the two known ids), and git trees cannot hold a `..` path component, so neither a repo-write attacker nor a malicious PR can plant such an entry — it needs control of the archive bytes (TLS-intercepting corporate proxy with a trusted root, CA mis-issuance, CDN compromise) or a future user-supplied `source`, which the generic `<owner>/<repo>/<subdir>#<ref>` parser is already written for. Two sub-claims are weaker than stated: the Windows backslash variant is probably moot because `files()` keys are documented as always forward-slashed, and in a bytes-controlling-MITM scenario the attacker already gets code execution from the scaffold itself (the CLI's outro tells the user to run `bun install && bun run dev`), so writing outside `dir` buys stealth and persistence rather than new capability. I keep MEDIUM because the project's stated threat model treats the create-mochi tarball as an untrusted supply-chain input and its own review guidance names this exact pattern ('archive extraction that joins an entry name onto an output directory… without rejecting `..` segments'), and it is not in the known-false-positive list. The recommended fix (normalize + reject `..`/absolute, assert containment with `path.resolve`, plus a fixture test) is cheap and correct.

The code does what the finding says — `transformPackageJson` (utils.ts:134-138) rewrites any `workspace:`-prefixed range to `'latest'` unless the key is exactly `mochi-framework` — but the dependency-confusion branch is unreachable, which the finding itself concedes ('currently latent rather than exploitable'). I read both shipped template manifests: `packages/minimal/package.json` declares `mochi-framework: workspace:*` and `svelte: ^5.57.3`; `packages/demos/package.json` declares `mochi-framework: workspace:*` plus only registry-versioned deps. `TEMPLATES` (templates.ts) contains exactly `minimal` and `demos`, so `minimal-rsvelte` (the one package that would pull `@mochi-framework/rsvelte`) is never scaffolded, and `addLintTooling` injects pinned caret ranges rather than workspace protocols. So today every scaffold takes the `mochiVersion` branch and the `'latest'` fallback is dead code. The hypothetical future regression is also not silent in the way described: the CLI regression harness scaffolds both templates and then runs `bun install`, `typecheck`, `lint` and `test` against them (.github/scripts/cli-regression-test.ts), so a template that grew a `workspace:*` dep on an unpublished private helper would fail resolution there, and the one plausible real-world case (`@mochi-framework/rsvelte` or `@mochi-framework/svelte-shaker`) is itself published to npm, so `'latest'` would resolve to the genuine package. That leaves only the secondary, non-security point — `'latest'` pins nothing, so scaffolds aren't reproducible — which is a legitimate nit but not the MEDIUM dependency-confusion vulnerability claimed. An allowlist is still a reasonable hardening, so the recommendation is worth keeping even though the finding does not stand as a vulnerability.

Both halves check out. `fetchLatestMochiVersion(signal?: AbortSignal)` (utils.ts:76-90) threads `signal` into the registry `fetch`, but a repo-wide grep shows exactly one caller — `create.ts:55`, `resolveMochiVersionRange(await fetchLatestMochiVersion())` — which passes nothing, and the only other reference is in `utils.test.ts` for `resolveMochiVersionRange`; the parameter is therefore dead code, which is precisely the kind of 'bounded on purpose, never actually bounded' defect worth reporting. The template `fetch` in download.ts:57 likewise carries only a User-Agent header, no signal. The try/catch in `fetchLatestMochiVersion` converts rejections into the `^0.1.1` fallback and cannot rescue a stall, and both calls sit behind `p.spinner()` ('Downloading … template'), so the user sees no output and no exit. One correction to the severity of the impact: Bun's `fetch` is not unbounded — it has a 300-second default idle timeout (per Bun's release notes, 'not for the cumulative time of the request, but rather the time between each chunk of data received', and since 1.4 one deadline for the whole response header block), so a fully dead connection rejects after ~5 minutes rather than hanging literally forever. A server that trickles body bytes can still extend it indefinitely, and a 5-minute silent spinner is itself a bad failure mode, so the recommendation (`AbortSignal.timeout(10_000)` on both calls) is right. The unvalidated `json.version` interpolation into `^${version}` straight into the scaffold's package.json is also accurate. BUG is the correct severity: this is robustness, not a security boundary.

I verified the asymmetry in the source and the hang in the dependency. `promptToggle` (cli.ts:146-160) returns the default when `!process.stdin.isTTY`, with a comment stating the reason; `promptDirectory` (105-125), `maybePromptForce` (127-144) and `promptTemplate` (162-176) call `p.text`/`p.confirm`/`p.select` with no such guard. In the installed `@clack/core@1.6.0`, `Prompt.prototype.prompt()` returns a Promise that is settled only by `this.once('submit')` / `this.once('cancel')` (plus an optional abort signal), and those states are reachable only from `onKeypress`; there is no handler for stdin `end`/`close`, so with a non-TTY stdin the call either blocks forever (an open pipe that never delivers a keypress) or the process drains the loop and exits silently having scaffolded nothing. The triggering conditions are exactly as described: no `[path]` argument, a non-empty target directory without `--force`, or no `--template`. The claim that CI never catches this is also right — .github/scripts/cli-regression-test.ts always spawns `bun create mochi@latest <dir> --template <t> --force`; notably it does *not* always pass `--eslint`/`--prettier`, which is why `promptToggle` needed its guard in the first place, strong evidence the non-TTY path is hit in practice. The secondary point is accurate too: all three helpers `process.exit(0)` on cancel/decline, so a scripted caller sees success after scaffolding nothing. This is a correctness/UX defect rather than a security issue, so BUG is the right severity.

Every mechanical claim verifies, but they do not add up to a vulnerability. I confirmed `buildLimiter` (Mochi.ts:801-828) returns `null` when `options.rateLimit` is unset and that packages/demos/src/index.ts sets none, that `KIND_POLICY.sse` (runtime/requestSetup.ts:65) has `timeout: true` so `server.timeout(req, 0)` disables Bun's per-request timeout, and that `stream.send` (Mochi.ts:~1388-1402) calls `controller.enqueue(frame)` without consulting `desiredSize`. I also confirmed the teardown is correct: the ReadableStream's `cancel()` runs `closeCallbacks`, and the route wires `stream.onClose(() => clearInterval(interval))`, so there is no timer leak. What is left is 'an unauthenticated endpoint has no rate limit', which is true of literally every route in this app (and of minimal), i.e. a hardening recommendation rather than an exploitable flaw: the per-connection cost is bounded and symmetric (one ~70-byte frame per 1.5 s, so ~170 KB/hour of queue growth in the pathological non-reading case, dwarfed by the socket itself), SSE streams legitimately need the request timeout disabled, and `await Bun.sleep(1500 + …)` on `/api/admin/products` holds a timer and a promise, not a thread or a worker — Bun serves thousands of such pending requests cheaply, so it is not the amplifier the finding describes. Decisively, this file is named in the project's own known-false-positive list ('packages/site/src/demos/* and the HN/admin/todo demos are demonstration code (hardcoded hunter2, shared mutable module state, no auth) — judge them as documentation, not product'), and the shared `stockPrice` module state the route depends on is flagged in-code as a 'demo simplification'. Bounding the stream's lifetime and adding a per-route limiter are still sensible, but there is no concrete attack here beyond flooding any public endpoint.

I traced the whole chain and every link holds. build.yml's `demos` matrix leg sets `dockerfile: Dockerfile`; that file's ENTRYPOINT is `exec bun run dev:${WORKSPACE}` → `bun --cwd=packages/demos run dev` → `NODE_ENV=development bun src/index.ts`, so index.ts:20 evaluates `development: true` in the internet-facing deployment (the Dockerfile header says so outright: 'Running in dev mode … so the debug bar and dev overlays are visible in the deployed environment'). From there: `runtime/errors.ts` sets `stack = development && thrown instanceof Error ? thrown.stack : undefined` and templates/DefaultError.svelte renders it in a `<pre>`, demos configures no `errorPage` or `handleError`, and `handleEnhancedError` (Mochi.ts:743) returns `err.message` instead of 'Internal Server Error' under development; `debugBarEnabled = development && (options.debugBar ?? true)` is true, mounting `buildClientStatsRoutes` (whose page renders every bundle output's `inputs[].path`, with the framework's own comment at Mochi.ts:787 calling that 'project structure and dependency names') and the page-cache admin at `/__mochi/admin/page-cache`; `emailViewerEnabled = development && transport === 'dev'` is true because email/config.ts defaults to the `dev` transport in development and demos configures no `email`, mounting `/_mochi/email` plus its attachment-streaming API; and `csrfCheckDefault` returns `null` with a `logger.warn` on an origin mismatch when development, so enforcement is log-only. `DEFAULT_ASSET_PREFIX` is `/_mochi` and internal page routes are registered on both slash forms, so `/_mochi/client/stats/` is unauthenticated and unconditionally reachable — no trigger needed — which is the finding's strongest leg; stack traces additionally need a 500, which is reachable but not reliably attacker-forced (`fetchItem`/`fetchUser` null-guard, though an upstream `fetch` throw or a malformed `res.json()` propagates). Two overstatements to note: the page-cache admin serves stub data with explicitly no-op purge actions, and demos never sends mail so its dev outbox is always empty. The important caveat is intentionality — the deployed debug bar links to both `/client/stats` and `/email` (debug-bar/BundlesPanel.svelte:59, MochiDebugBar.svelte:136), so mounting them follows from a documented choice, and packages/site has the same exposure with only an SEO-motivated mitigation (lib/debugBarEncode.ts). Even so this is not in the known-false-positive list, the threat model explicitly says 'Dev-only code reaching production matters here: the email viewer streams arbitrary attachment bytes, the client-stats page discloses bundle inputs and paths', and the CSRF degradation is plainly an unintended side effect of the single flag. MEDIUM stands for the aggregate (CWE-489-style active debug code plus unauthenticated path/structure disclosure), and the recommended decoupling of the toolbar from full development mode is the right fix.

The code reading is accurate — index.ts:27 resolves `proxy.origin` to `process.env.MOCHI_ORIGIN || http://localhost:${PORT}`, `MOCHI_ORIGIN` appears nowhere in the demos deploy path (not in Dockerfile, not in build.yml's demos leg), `buildPublicUrl` (runtime/proxy.ts:47-54) would then rebuild `event.url` against that bogus origin for every request, and support/src/index.ts:74 does guard the same variable in a `mochi:init` hook while demos does not. But the asserted consequence cannot occur, and the blockers are independent and all verifiable. First, demos has no server-side form actions at all: grepping packages/demos/src for `actions:`, `fail(`, `success(` and `method="post"` returns nothing, and the single `<form>` (todo/TodoApp.svelte:87) is a client-side island handler with `e.preventDefault()`, so no request ever reaches the CSRF comparison. Second, the deployed image runs in development mode (verified under F6), where `csrfCheckDefault` only warns on a mismatch instead of returning 403 — the finding concedes this masking. Third, nothing consumes `event.url.origin`: demos builds every canonical/og URL from the hardcoded `SITE_URL = 'https://demos.mochi.fast'` (lib/baseMetaTags.ts:3) or literal `https://demos.mochi.fast${url.pathname}` strings, the HN redirect uses raw `req.url` rather than the configured origin, and a grep of packages/mochi/src finds no framework code emitting `url.origin` into client-visible output. Fourth, trailing-slash redirects are path-only, as the finding itself notes (trailingSlash.ts `permanentRedirect` sets a bare `Location`). So with `MOCHI_ORIGIN` unset nothing observable breaks — there is no malfunction to classify as a bug, only a missing defensive assertion, and the localhost fallback is the documented dev ergonomic used identically by support and by newsletter/config.ts (and shipped verbatim in the create-mochi demos template). Adding the `mochi:init` check and setting the variable in the deploy config is still worthwhile hygiene, and would matter the moment demos grows a form action, but as filed the finding describes a condition with no current effect.
